clue.text: Found his stable after journeying

indicators.note: journeying sets the words his stable travelling about, so their letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone discovers their horse box after a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' looks like the past tense of find, but it is the verb meaning to set up. 'journeying' signals the anagram of HIS STABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To found an institution is to set it up and get it going.

clue.text: I've gone to live abroad, opportunely chasing former partner

indicators.note: chasing puts the word for opportunely behind the former partner, running after it

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
pat means at just the right moment, as in an answer coming pat

explanation.surface: An emigrant explains they left the country, conveniently following an ex-spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: An emigrant is someone who has left their own country to settle overseas.

clue.text: Shaving is certainly following fashion

indicators.note: following puts the word for certainly after the word for fashion

parts.note: ton is an old word for high fashion or the fashionable set
sure, as in 'sure, I'll come', means certainly

explanation.surface: A man insists that shaving is definitely the current trend.
explanation.definitionFit: A monk's shaved crown is the classic example of a head shaved for religious reasons.

clue.text: Refuses to handle sickly pale bird

parts.note: to black goods is a trade-union term for refusing to handle them during a dispute
wan means pale and ill-looking

explanation.surface: Someone will not touch an unhealthy-looking white bird.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'black' goods is a British trade-union term: workers in a dispute refuse to handle them.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark-plumaged swan native to Australia is a species of waterfowl.

clue.text: Wayward mill girl's bloody rude

indicators.note: wayward means straying, so the letters of mill wander out of order

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name; the 's is a link
something bloody is red with blood

explanation.surface: A factory girl is being thoroughly rude, with a British swear word thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wayward' turns MILL into ILLM. 'bloody' reads as the British swear word, but here it means red, coloured by blood.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lacking courtesy and good manners behaves impolitely.

clue.text: Sock for skier, perhaps

definitions.meaning: to sock someone is to punch or strike them
in cricket a skier is a stroke that sends the ball high into the air, one kind of stroke

explanation.surface: A piece of hosiery for someone on the slopes.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures footwear for a skier; in cricket a 'skier' is a ball struck high into the air.
explanation.definitionFit: A punch and a cricket stroke are both strikes, one with the fist and one with the bat.

clue.text: Crowd spirit dogs special constable

indicators.note: dogs means follows closely, so the spirit comes after the constable

parts.note: SC is the abbreviation for special constable, a British volunteer police officer
rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane

explanation.surface: A ghost haunts a part-time police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: A special constable is a volunteer part-time police officer in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A disorderly throng of people pressing together is a jostling mass.

clue.text: Rogue's trick with penny

parts.note: a scam is a swindle or trick
p is the abbreviation for penny in British money

explanation.surface: A con artist's ruse involves a single coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A mischievous rascal or ne'er-do-well is a rogue in the lighter sense.

clue.text: Lock phone that's rented to tenant

parts.note: to ring someone is to phone them
a property let is one rented out to a tenant

explanation.surface: A landlord supplies a door lock and phone with the flat he rents out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock' suggests a door fastening; here it is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A curl of hair hanging down is a lock in the sense of a tress.

clue.text: Slam metro reconstruction for confused state of affairs

indicators.note: reconstruction means building again, so the letters of slam metro are rearranged

explanation.surface: Critics attack rebuilding of the underground as chaotic.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirlpool used figuratively stands for a scene of turmoil and chaos.

clue.text: Chess attack completely surrounds bishop for game

parts.note: a pin is a chess tactic pinning a piece to one behind it
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
all, as in 'all alone', means completely

explanation.surface: A chess move wholly hems in the bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess vocabulary points to a board game, but the game is an arcade one.
explanation.definitionFit: An arcade amusement where a steel ball is flipped round a sloping table is a game.

clue.text: Shower appearing in TV's first broadcast "apprentice"

indicators.note: appearing in puts the shower inside the other piece
broadcast means the letter is spoken, so its name is written out
the first letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: the first letter of TV is T
a shower is a short fall of rain

explanation.surface: A downpour features in the first episode of a TV series about an apprentice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' signals that the letter is spoken, so it is spelt as its name. The quotation marks round 'apprentice' hint at the TV show The Apprentice, the 'first broadcast' of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone learning a trade under supervision is a learner or novice.

clue.text: Rice, not dessert, in school food trolley

indicators.note: in places the letter left from rice inside the school food

parts.note: tuck is British school slang for snacks and sweets, as in a tuck shop

indicators.note: not tells us to take the dessert out of the word rice

parts.note: ice, as in an ice cream, is a dessert

explanation.surface: A school trolley carries rice pudding left without the sweet course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not dessert' removes ICE from RICE, leaving R. TUCK is British school slang for snacks, sold at a tuck shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A porter's handcart or wheeled platform for moving goods is a kind of trolley.

clue.text: After a harvest, grain store turned into a place of high security

indicators.note: after means the turned grain store follows a and harvest

parts.note: a crop is the harvest of a season

indicators.note: turned means the grain store is read backwards

parts.note: a silo is a tower for storing grain

explanation.surface: Once the crop is in, a granary is converted into a secure lock-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses SILO to OLIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A citadel on a hilltop, like that of Athens, is a fortified stronghold set high up.

clue.text: Upset ketch or another vessel?

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so the letters of ketch or are tipped into a new order

parts.note: a boat is another kind of craft besides a ketch

explanation.surface: A sailor wonders whether to capsize a ketch or some other craft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' turns KETCH OR into ROCKTHE; with BOAT the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To destabilise a craft is the idiom for causing trouble by disturbing a settled situation.

clue.text: Fish privately, as this would show?

indicators.note: the clue says that as plus this would show privately, so taking as away leaves this

parts.note: an aside is a remark made privately, so aside means privately
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone fishes discreetly, wondering what would reveal it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'privately' is ASIDE, which is AS followed by 'this' (the answer), so removing AS leaves the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A European freshwater fish of the carp family is a crossword staple.

clue.text: Keeping mum surrounded by asinine vernacular

indicators.note: surrounded by puts the word for mum inside the word for asinine

parts.note: asinine means foolish, like an ass
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Someone keeps quiet when surrounded by foolish chatter in the local dialect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeping mum' reads as staying silent, but mum is MA. 'Keeping' links the two.
explanation.definitionFit: Language natural to native speakers, using everyday expressions, is vernacular in style.

clue.text: Turn cold, needing warmer jacket

parts.note: to wind a handle is to turn it
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
a heater is something that warms

explanation.surface: The weather turns cold and someone needs a heater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'warmer' looks like an adjective but is a noun, a thing that warms.
explanation.definitionFit: A light outer coat that keeps out wind is a type of jacket.

clue.text: I hope rule goes abroad!

indicators.note: goes abroad means the letters of I hope rule travel away from their order

explanation.surface: A supporter of the EU hopes governance will move to the Continent.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: such a person would hope that rule passes to Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: An enthusiast for the European Union wants more government from Brussels.

clue.text: One reduces waste at home, certain to suffer otherwise

parts.note: in means at home, as in 'staying in'

indicators.note: to suffer means the word certain is damaged and its letters are rearranged

parts.note: or, as in 'hurry or you'll miss it', means otherwise

explanation.surface: Someone cuts down waste at home, knowing they will suffer if they don't.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to suffer' turns CERTAIN into CINERAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A furnace that burns rubbish turns it to ash, cutting the bulk of refuse.

clue.text: Cheat's hard to vouch for

parts.note: a con is a cheat or swindle; the 's is a link
firm means hard, not soft

explanation.surface: A swindler's tough to vouch for.
explanation.definitionFit: To corroborate something is to state that it is true.

clue.text: What Dick Whittington had in pantomime?

definitions.text: What Dick Whittington had in pantomime?

parts.words: What Dick Whittington had in pantomime?
parts.note: in the pantomime the hero Dick Whittington is famous for his companion, a male cat

explanation.surface: A question about the story of Dick Whittington as staged in pantomime.
explanation.walkthrough: Dick Whittington is a British pantomime hero who goes to London with his cat; a male cat is called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The usual word for a male cat fits Dick's famous feline companion.

clue.text: Primate, one who delays leaving, wanting a right to become saint

indicators.note: to become says the right is changed into the saint

parts.note: a tarrier is one who tarries, lingering before going

explanation.surface: A primate dawdles at leaving, needing an upgrade to sainthood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting a right to become saint' changes one R of TARRIER into S. Tarrier is a rare word for someone who tarries.
explanation.definitionFit: A small big-eyed tree-dwelling animal of Southeast Asia belongs to the primate order.

clue.text: Give rough treatment to the French after crew had come across middle of channel

indicators.note: after puts the French article at the end

parts.note: to man a ship is to crew it

indicators.note: come across means the word had spans the letter taken from channel

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: middle of picks the central letter of channel

parts.note: le is French for the

explanation.surface: Sailors crossing the Channel to France get rough handling.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a Channel crossing; here the middle letter of 'channel' goes inside HAD.
explanation.definitionFit: To shove or push someone about physically is to handle them roughly.

clue.text: What anno domini at last will make one?

definitions.text: What anno domini at last will make one?

parts.note: AD is the abbreviation for anno domini
ult., short for ultimo, means last month, from old business letters

explanation.surface: A question about what the passing years will eventually turn someone into.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anno domini' is jokey slang for advancing age, so the years finally make one a grown-up. ULT is an old business-letter abbreviation for last month.
explanation.definitionFit: A fully grown person has reached maturity through the passing of years.

clue.text: Share's face value is yielding capital

parts.note: par is the nominal or face value of a share
taken as written

explanation.surface: A stockbroker notes that a share's nominal worth is yielding capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like financial money in this surface, but it is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: The French seat of government is a national capital city.

clue.text: Is spinning recently introduced fibre

indicators.note: spinning means the word is turns around to read backwards

parts.note: something new has only recently been introduced

explanation.surface: A new fibre is being spun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinning' turns IS into SI.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendon is a tough cord of fibrous tissue joining muscle to bone.

clue.text: Popular champion of native group standing outside united nations

indicators.note: standing outside means the native group goes round the united nations

parts.note: a tribe is a group of native people

explanation.surface: A people's champion from an indigenous group is kept out of the UN.
explanation.walkthrough: In ancient Rome a tribune was an official who protected the interests of the common people.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman officer elected to defend plebeians is a champion of the people.

clue.text: As a cockney might do with this?

definitions.text: As a cockney might do with this?

parts.words: As a cockney might do with this?
parts.note: a cockney drops the first letter of the verb for listening, and does that listening with this organ

explanation.surface: A question about what a Londoner might do with something.
explanation.walkthrough: A cockney (a working-class Londoner) drops initial H, so the verb for listening comes out as this organ's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The organ of hearing is what anyone listens with, cockney or not.

clue.text: Nought's secure about arms judgement

parts.note: nought is zero, the letter O; the 's is a link
to pinion someone is to bind their arms to hold them fast

explanation.surface: Zero is secure regarding weapons, someone judges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arms' suggests weapons, but it means the limbs: to pinion is to tie someone's arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A view or belief formed about something is one's considered judgement.

clue.text: Mostly carefully search alien body found in space

indicators.note: mostly means the word for carefully search loses its last letter

parts.note: to comb an area is to search it carefully
ET, the film's extra-terrestrial, is an alien

explanation.surface: Searchers carefully comb for an alien body found in space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' drops the B from COMB.
explanation.definitionFit: An icy object orbiting the Sun with a glowing tail is a celestial body.

clue.text: The way horses may be ridden in town?

definitions.text: The way horses may be ridden in town?

parts.words: The way horses may be ridden in town?
parts.note: the clue asks for a route; a horse track in a London park fits, the 'way' being a road

explanation.surface: A question about how one should ride horses in a city.
explanation.walkthrough: Rotten Row is the famous riding track along the south side of Hyde Park in London. 'The way' looks like a manner of riding but is a road.
explanation.definitionFit: The London bridleway through Hyde Park is a route for riding horses in the city.
